patterns.usage_note: Colloquial contraction of ても/でも: だって appears after ta-stems that voice the た (読んだって, 急いだって) and たって elsewhere (食べたって, 話したって). Its work in this concessive class is to grant an action and deny that it helps; the bare noun＋だって of 子供だって知っている is the separate 'even X' particle of the extreme-example class. It belongs to everyday speech and is rarely written outside dialogue; the formal counterparts are ても and にしても.

examples.ruby: 今[いま]から呼[よ]んだって、もう間[ま]に合[あ]わないだろう。
examples.english: Calling him now isn't going to get him here in time.

examples.ruby: 傘[かさ]を持[も]って行[い]ったって、この風[かぜ]じゃ意味[いみ]がないよ。
examples.english: Even if you take an umbrella, it's no use in wind like this.

examples.ruby: いくら考[かんが]えたって、いい案[あん]なんて浮[う]かばない。
examples.english: No matter how hard I think, no good ideas come to me.

patterns.usage_note: A spoken-register 〜としても built on とする + たって: it supposes a scenario that has not come about, and the main clause typically denies that the supposition changes anything. The 確定 sibling instead grants a claim someone has actually put forward. It attaches to plain forms, including だ and た. Its sibling にしたって picks up a case rather than framing an explicit supposition.

examples.ruby: 明日[あした]から始[はじ]めるとしたって、準備[じゅんび]がまるで足[た]りない。
examples.english: Even supposing we start tomorrow, we're nowhere near ready.

examples.ruby: 薬[くすり]が効[き]いたとしたって、この熱[ねつ]では明日[あした]も休[やす]むしかない。
examples.english: Even granting the medicine worked, with a fever like this I'll have to take tomorrow off too.

examples.ruby: 冗談[じょうだん]だとしたって、その言[い]い方[かた]はひどすぎる。
examples.english: Even granting it was a joke, that's a terrible way to put it.

patterns.usage_note: Colloquial 〜にしても used to grant a case that has not actually come about: you suppose it for the sake of argument (手伝うにしたって, 雨が降るにしたって) and the main clause says it changes nothing. The 確定 sibling starts instead from a real, already-established case (部長にしたって), and としたって frames the supposition explicitly with とする. The formal counterparts are にしても／にしろ／にせよ.

examples.ruby: 安[やす]く買[か]えるにしたって、これ以上[いじょう]物[もの]は増[ふ]やせない。
examples.english: Even supposing I could get it cheap, I've no room for another thing.

examples.ruby: 手伝[てつだ]うにしたって、これだけの量[りょう]は今日[きょう]中[じゅう]に終[お]わらない。
examples.english: Even if I pitch in, there's no finishing this much today.

examples.ruby: 明日[あした]雨[あめ]が降[ふ]るにしたって、準備[じゅんび]だけは進[すす]めておこう。
examples.english: Even if it does rain tomorrow, let's at least get the preparations done.

patterns.usage_note: A concessive hypothetical whose main clause almost always says the effort changes nothing (変わらない, 無駄だ, 〜ない), often set up by 今さら/いくら/どんなに. Here the effort is entertained as a supposition; the 確定 sibling covers the same form where the pointless effort is one actually under way or being urged right now. Because the main clause describes how things stand rather than what the speaker will do, commands and requests rarely follow it. The full form is 〜たところで／〜だところで; in casual speech ところ reduces to とこ, giving 走ったとこで, 騒いだとこで. The だ variant appears after ta-stems in ん/い (読んだ, 急いだ).

examples.ruby: そんなに水[みず]をやったところで、この鉢[はち]の花[はな]は元気[げんき]にならないよ。
examples.english: Watering it that much isn't going to perk up the flowers in this pot.

examples.ruby: ここで騒[さわ]いだとこで、決[き]まったことはひっくり返[かえ]らないよ。
examples.english: Kicking up a fuss here isn't going to overturn what's already been decided.

examples.ruby: 今[いま]さら言[い]い訳[わけ]を並[なら]べたところで、信用[しんよう]は戻[もど]らない。
examples.english: Piling up excuses at this point isn't going to win back anyone's trust.

patterns.usage_note: An emphatic concessive on the volitional/conjectural form (行こうとも, 険しかろうとも), typically reinforced by たとえ or どんなに. It is written and declamatory in register, stiffer than 〜うと and far stiffer than colloquial ても. Dropping the も gives 〜うと, the same meaning a shade lighter.

examples.ruby: どんなに時間[じかん]がかかろうとも、最後[さいご]までやり抜[ぬ]く。
examples.english: However long it takes, I will see this through to the end.

examples.ruby: たとえ全[すべ]てを失[うしな]おうとも、この信念[しんねん]だけは曲[ま]げない。
examples.english: Even if I lose everything, this one conviction I will not bend.

examples.ruby: 周[まわ]りに何[なに]を言[い]われようとも、妹[いもうと]は毎朝[まいあさ]の練習[れんしゅう]をやめなかった。
examples.english: No matter what anyone said to her, my sister never once skipped her morning practice.

patterns.usage_note: Takes the same volitional attachment as 〜うとも, but が colors it with the speaker's indifference: whatever happens, it makes no difference to me. It is a shade more conversational than うとも and is the form that most readily doubles up (行こうが行くまいが, 雨が降ろうが槍が降ろうが). Where the sibling entry favours the paired frames and brushes a condition aside as beside the point in advance, this entry's typical shape is a single condition answered by the speaker's own resolve or dismissal.

examples.ruby: 誰[だれ]が反対[はんたい]しようが、この企画[きかく]は必[かなら]ず通[とお]してみせる。
examples.english: I don't care who objects; I'm getting this project approved.

examples.ruby: 結果[けっか]がどう出[で]ようが、私[わたし]は自分[じぶん]の選択[せんたく]を悔[く]やまない。
examples.english: However it turns out, I won't regret the choice I made.

examples.ruby: 値段[ねだん]が上[あ]がろうが、この味噌[みそ]だけは他[ほか]に替[か]えられない。
examples.english: The price can climb all it likes; this is the one miso I won't trade for another.

patterns.usage_note: The formal counterpart of 〜にしても; にせよ is stiffer still, and both lean written. Doubled, it lists alternatives and means 'whether … or …'; used singly it concedes a supposition before the speaker presses an objection or a demand. The 確定 sibling instead concedes something already established (断られたにしろ). It attaches to nouns and plain forms, and often follows an interrogative (誰にしろ, 何にしろ) meaning 'whoever/whatever'.

examples.ruby: 賛成[さんせい]するにしろ反対[はんたい]するにしろ、理由[りゆう]は述[の]べてほしい。
examples.english: Whether you're for it or against it, I'd like to hear your reasons.

examples.ruby: 新人[しんじん]にしろ、この程度[ていど]の確認[かくにん]は怠[おこた]るべきでない。
examples.english: Even if you're new here, you shouldn't be skipping a check this basic.

examples.ruby: 引[ひ]っ越[こ]すにしろ、この部屋[へや]の荷物[にもつ]は半分[はんぶん]に減[へ]らすしかない。
examples.english: Even if you do move, there's nothing for it but to cut what's in this room by half.
